stem:
Aarav's uncle reports that nilgai have begun entering crop fields after a dry season left forest grass scarce and nearby streams almost empty.

Which claim best explains why the animals moved?

options.text: When food plants and water become scarce in the natural habitat, nilgai move into farms in search of resources.
Nilgai enter farms for company even when forest grass and streams remain plentiful.
Farms create extra forest grass and fuller streams, which then pull the nilgai in.
Forest cover, rainfall, and water have no link to where nilgai find food and water.

teacher.key_rationale: Scarcity of vegetation and water in the natural habitat drives animals into farms. Preferring farms while resources remain plentiful drops the scarcity condition. Saying farms create forest grass and water reverses cause and effect. Denying any link stretches past the habitat-resource rule.
